sources.supports: Regional ice-sheet and marginal feature-class context, distinguishing glacier, fjord and settlement names from evidence of a named river.

sources.title: Compendio de información geográfica municipal 2010. Hermosillo, Sonora
sources.page: PDF pp. 6–7, Localidades e Infraestructura para el Transporte and Relieve; hydrography table on PDF pp. 3–4.

correspondence.finding: The selected beginning approaches from the southwest through the Santa Inês–Conceição setting. ANA describes the principal sequence as beginning with Piancó in Santa Inês, while Figure 5 labels Riacho Santa Inês in the far southwestern feeder setting. The exact feeder-to-Piancó name transition is left unassigned.

The route continues through Itaporanga and Piancó to the Curema/Mãe-d’Água reservoir setting at Coremas, then north toward the Pombal junction. The maps distinguish this approach from the western upper Piranhas through São José de Piranhas and the separate Peixe contribution.

Beyond the Pombal setting the selection follows the mapped middle Piranhas through Paulista, São Bento and Jardim de Piranhas toward Jucurutu. ANA explicitly places the name Piranhas after the Piancó confluence; the modeled fragment boundary is not treated as that name boundary.

The middle piece crosses the Armando Ribeiro Gonçalves reservoir corridor before continuing toward Assú. ANA identifies the downstream change from Piranhas to Açu at this dam. Reservoir and channel name scopes are retained separately.

The final sequence follows the lower Açu through the Assú–Ipanguaçu and Alto do Rodrigues–Pendências setting toward coastal Macau. Official maps show the Atlantic receiving setting and a branching lower network; no exact mouth or individual estuarine distributary is assigned to the selected endpoint.

The southern selected beginning lies in the feeder-and-lake country southwest of the Champdoré–Tudor setting, then continues north toward the upper Baleine corridor. CEHQ distinguishes that corridor from the De Pas and George drainage to its east. The first selected feeder and small headwater waterbodies remain unnamed; neither a neighboring lake label nor the modeled mainstem role establishes an official river source.

The northward route reaches the Jeannin–Ninawawe lake setting before bending northwest. The ministry map embedded in the Kativik plan separately labels Lac Jeannin, Lac Ninawawe and the downstream Rivière à la Baleine; the adjoining description places the Lac-Jeannin territory in the Baleine basin. This supports the lake-to-river corridor without assigning exact entry/exit vertices or extending a river hydronym across every lake passage.

Beyond the broad westward bend, the selected mainstem follows the sustained northwest-to-north corridor labeled Rivière à la Baleine. The maps distinguish the parallel Marralik and Qurlutuq systems to the east and the False/Koksoak setting to the west; the connected route does not switch into those neighboring rivers.

The two tributary fragments form one western connected branch, approaching the mainstem from southern lake country and then continuing north to the confluence. CEHQ labels this middle-to-lower corridor Rivière Wheeler, and the Kativik plan independently names the Baleine–Wheeler confluence. The two fragments are not two separately established river names; their initial small feeder and exact lake passages remain unassigned.

The last selected piece continues into the lower Baleine coastal approach on the southern side of Ungava Bay. CEHQ and the Kativik Marralik map show the Baleine connection toward that bay separately from the neighboring Marralik corridor. The selected endpoint is not asserted to mark the surveyed mouth, the full estuarine channel or the freshwater–tidal limit.

correspondence: The complete single selected fragment was inspected from its southern interior endpoint along the long nearly northward leg to a short northwestward bend and westward terminal hook. No additional tributary fragment is present.

The long southern and middle portions lie on mapped Inland Ice. The short northern bends approach the adjoining marginal terrain in the broader Sherard Osborn Fjord–Victoria Fjord setting. The map graticule and ice/land arrangement support this regional feature-class reading, without assigning an exact terminal stream, glacier or fjord boundary.

The readable source does not establish a natural river name for the complete modeled route. Nearby glacier, land or fjord labels cannot supply a uniform river identity or prove subglacial connectivity; the scope hold does not imply that all local marginal waterways are unnamed.

Ice-surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs and sub-ice bedrock contours describe ice and terrain rather than named river channels. Historical mapping does not establish current ice margins, flow direction or connectivity along the model path.

correspondence.finding: The northern approach lies southeast of Cananea and continues toward Bacoachi on the Río Sonora side of the headwater setting. Cananea mapping separately labels the western Bacanuchi drainage; no precise feeder name is assigned to the first modeled reach.

The long southward valley course matches Bacoachi, Arizpe, Sinoquipe, Banámichi, Huépac, Aconchi and Baviácora. Readable Sonora labels and the sequence of bends support the river corridor rather than municipality or basin membership alone.

Near Mazocahui the course turns west and southwest through the Puerta del Sol–Ures setting toward Topahue and Hermosillo. San Miguel de Horcasitas approaches from the north and is separately mapped, not an alias for this selected upstream branch.

The Hermosillo approach passes the Ingeniero Rodolfo Félix Valdés (El Molinito) and Abelardo L. Rodríguez reservoir settings in that order. The municipal map labels Río Sonora between the storage settings; the water surfaces and precise modeled crossings are not assigned a uniform river name.

The terminal extension crosses the plain west of Hermosillo toward the Bahía de Kino–Punta Blanca coastal setting. Official maps distinguish Canal Hermosillo, Río Sonora-labelled reaches and other plain channels; this regional correspondence does not establish a single named channel, an exact current mouth or uninterrupted surface flow along the modeled extension.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
